entities.name: Tracking Auditor
entities.description: A web-based analytics tracking audit tool that connects to Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, and optionally Google Ads via OAuth to analyse a tracking setup and generate a scored audit report exported to Google Drive.

hasChunks.text: Tracking Auditor is a web-based tool that connects to your Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, and optionally Google Ads accounts (via Google OAuth) to analyse your tracking setup and generate a scored audit report. The report is exported to your Google Drive as a Google Doc and Google Sheet.
Audit your GA4, GTM, and Google Ads tracking stack in minutes. Scored across consent, data quality, and conversion integrity.
Connect your GA4, GTM, and Google Ads accounts and get a scored audit like this one — with a client-ready export — in under two minutes.

entities.name: Tracking Audit
entities.description: Tracking Auditor's named process for connecting to a GTM container, GA4 property, and optionally Google Ads account, then scoring findings across five dimensions: Consent Architecture, Cookie Classification, GTM Tag Governance, GA4 Event Quality, and Conversion Integrity.

hasChunks.text: Generate scored findings across consent architecture, data quality, GTM governance, event quality, and conversion integrity.
Tracking Auditor provides automated analysis based on data available via Google APIs. Audit results are informational and may not capture every issue with your tracking setup.

entities.name: Consent Architecture
entities.description: A scored dimension in Tracking Auditor's audit that measures how well a site's consent configuration signals user choices to Google tags, including whether Consent Mode v2 is correctly implemented.

hasChunks.text:
Consent Architecture

58
Consent Mode v2 is not configured — resolve the consent gap before relying on this setup for GDPR compliance

entities.name: Cookie Classification
entities.description: A scored dimension in Tracking Auditor's audit that assesses how cookies present on a site are categorised and disclosed relative to consent requirements.

hasChunks.text:
Cookie Classification

72

entities.name: GTM Tag Governance
entities.description: A scored dimension in Tracking Auditor's audit that evaluates the cleanliness and quality of a Google Tag Manager container configuration, including unused triggers and legacy tags.

hasChunks.text:
GTM Tag Governance

64
The GTM container has 12 triggers that are not referenced by any tag. They have no data impact but add clutter and make the container harder to audit and maintain.

entities.name: GA4 Event Quality
entities.description: A scored dimension in Tracking Auditor's audit that rates the accuracy and deduplication of GA4 event data, including detection of duplicate events and misconfigured Enhanced Measurement settings.

hasChunks.text:
GA4 Event Quality

45
GA4 Enhanced Measurement and a GTM tag are both sending the scroll event, so every scroll is counted twice. This inflates engagement metrics and any audience or report built on scroll depth.

entities.name: Conversion Integrity
entities.description: A scored dimension in Tracking Auditor's audit that measures the reliability of conversion tracking data, including detection of duplicate purchase events and misconfigured Google Ads attribution settings.

hasChunks.text:
Conversion Integrity

55

Your purchase event is firing twice on the order confirmation page — 34 of 412 transactions in the last 30 days were recorded as duplicates. This inflates reported revenue by roughly 8% and corrupts the conversion data that Google Ads Smart Bidding uses to optimise spend.

entities.name: Consent Mode v2
entities.description: Google's framework for signalling a user's consent state to Google tags before they fire, enabling conversion modelling for users who decline consent and supporting GDPR compliance.

hasChunks.text: GA4 and Google Ads tags are not receiving consent signals from your cookie banner. Tags may fire before a visitor has granted consent, and you lose access to Google's conversion modelling that recovers data from users who decline.
Implement Consent Mode v2 in GTM with a Consent Initialisation trigger, and confirm your CMP pushes default and update consent states before any tags fire.

entities.name: Google Tag Manager
entities.description: Google's tag management platform, connected read-only by Tracking Auditor to fetch container configuration — tags, triggers, variables, and consent settings — for analysis.

hasChunks.text: Google Tag Manager (read-only) — To fetch your GTM container configuration — tags, triggers, variables, and consent settings — for analysis.

entities.name: Google Analytics 4
entities.description: Google's analytics platform, connected read-only by Tracking Auditor to fetch property configuration and run data quality checks against traffic data from the last 30 days.

hasChunks.text: Google Analytics (read-only) — To fetch your GA4 property configuration and run data quality checks against your traffic data from the last 30 days.

entities.name: Google Ads
entities.description: Google's advertising platform, optionally connected read-only by Tracking Auditor to audit conversion actions, campaign bidding strategies, and auto-tagging status.

hasChunks.text: Google Ads (read-only, optional) — To fetch your conversion actions, campaign bidding strategies, and auto-tagging status for the Ads section of the audit. Only requested if you choose to include Google Ads in your audit.

Google Ads auto-tagging is switched off, so paid clicks arrive without a GCLID and are misattributed as 'direct' traffic in GA4. You have 3 campaigns running Target ROAS — these are bidding on incomplete attribution data, wasting budget.

entities.name: Google OAuth
entities.description: The OAuth 2.0 authentication protocol used by Tracking Auditor to request read-only access to a user's Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, Google Drive, and optionally Google Ads accounts.

hasChunks.text: Tracking Auditor connects to your Google account using OAuth 2.0. We request the following permissions and use them solely to generate your tracking audit report.

OAuth tokens are stored in an encrypted session cookie in your browser for the duration of your session. Tokens are used to make API calls on your behalf and are not retained on our servers beyond the active session.

entities.name: Duplicate Purchase Event
entities.description: A tracking error where a GA4 purchase event fires more than once per transaction on the order confirmation page, inflating reported revenue and corrupting the conversion data used by Google Ads Smart Bidding.

hasChunks.text: Your purchase event is firing twice on the order confirmation page — 34 of 412 transactions in the last 30 days were recorded as duplicates. This inflates reported revenue by roughly 8% and corrupts the conversion data that Google Ads Smart Bidding uses to optimise spend.

Add a transaction_id-based deduplication check, or move the purchase tag onto a single trigger that fires once per completed order. Verify in GA4 DebugView that purchase fires exactly once per transaction.

context.condition: when a purchase tag fires more than once per transaction
duplicate event firing inflates reported revenue and event counts
